title: createInstantSearchRouterNext without SSR clears state when filters are applied
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

Clicking refinements briefly shows the filtered items, and then reverts the selection when using createInstantSearchRouterNext in client-side only mode.

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/jmotes-lapero/algolia-issues-repro
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run dev`
4. Try to apply facet filters

### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/s/github/jmotes-lapero/algolia-issues-repro

### 💭 Expected behavior

Checkboxes should persist and search results filtered by the new facet value.

### Package version

react-instantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs 6.40.1

### Operating system

Ubuntu Linux

### Browser

Chrome

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

comments.body:
Hi @jmotes-lapero,

Thank you for raising this issue.

I had a look, and the issue is because the `fallbackComponent` provided to `DynamicWidgets` is an inline component, so the reference changes each render which makes it remount thus clearing the state.
Our [documentation does show the proper usage](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/widgets/dynamic-facets/react-hooks/#widget-param-fallbackcomponent) although maybe we should mention it should be a stable reference.

So the problem is not related to the router itself but the usage of `DynamicWidgets`, and can be fixed just by changing this line : 
```diff
<DynamicWidgets
  facets={[]} 
-  fallbackComponent={(props) => <RefinementList {...props} />}
+  fallbackComponent={RefinementList}
/>
```
My guess is maybe you're seeing it now because `react-instantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs` does a `push` with the Next.js router, which rerenders the whole page whereas before it wouldn't and `fallbackComponent` would have stayed the same.

Thanks for the quick reply @aymeric-giraudet! This did indeed fix my minimal reproduction.

~~However, the issue originated in a codebase that doesn't use DynamicWidgets at all - it just loops over an array of hardcoded refinements and renders a custom `<RefinementList />` (that's built using the useRefinements hook) directly. Any ideas on how to fix it there? Do I need to add the DynamicWidgets component to my main project?~~

Edit: Nevermind! I'll try to create another minimal reproduction that illustrates the issue there. I tried adding a simple loop to this repo and it still worked fine.
As long as the component references are stable, no inline components, I don't think there should be an issue :)
Just wanted to chime in and say I'm also experiencing this issue using custom `RefinementList` components
@lewisflude I traced my last problem with this to some inline dynamic component binding logic that I had in a parent component.  Not sure if that helps you but thought I'd mention just incase :)
Thanks @jmotes! Is there any chance you could go into more detail?
